rationale: Extensive natural history and prenatal neuroimaging studies confirm that classic pontocerebellar hypoplasia (specifically PCH2A caused by TSEN54 variants) typically presents with head circumference and general biometrics well within normal reference ranges both prenatally and at birth. Microcephaly in classic PCH develops postnatally as a progressive deceleration of cranial growth, often only crossing below abnormal thresholds (-2 to -3 SD) months to years after birth. Furthermore, routine mid-gestation prenatal neurosonography frequently fails to detect pontocerebellar hypoplasia or dysgenesis. Consequently, the presence of normal prenatal head biometry and normal routine neurosonography cannot serve as an exclusionary discriminator to differentiate PLAA-related progressive microcephaly and brain anomalies from classic pontocerebellar hypoplasia.

evidence.text: In a homogeneous cohort of 33 PCH2A patients homozygous for the TSEN54 p.A307S mutation, head circumference, weight, and length were mostly within normal limits at birth and progressively slowed postnatally, reaching severe microcephaly averaging -5.58 SD by age 5 years.

source.title: Natural course of pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2A
source.quote: Weight, length and head circumference, mostly in the normal range at birth, became abnormal, especially head circumference (-5.58 SD at age 5 yrs).

evidence.text: Detailed serial prenatal ultrasound in IVF twins with TSEN54-associated PCH2 failed to detect cerebellar abnormalities in utero; both infants were born normocephalic (50th percentile) and crossed percentiles downward to microcephaly (<3rd percentile) by 6 months postnatally.

evidence.text: In a clinical and neuroimaging cohort of 24 children with pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2, 18 were completely normocephalic at birth, developing microcephaly only subsequently during infancy.

source.title: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2: variability in clinical and imaging findings
source.quote: Eighteen were normocephalic at birth, but all developed microcephaly during infancy.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 65 children with confirmed PCH2A, specialized prenatal ultrasound performed between 12 and 32 gestational weeks detected only unspecific cerebellar abnormalities in 4 of 21 cases evaluated, demonstrating that ultrasound screening frequently fails to detect classic PCH.

source.title: Diagnostic Clues and Pitfalls in Pontocerebellar ...
source.quote: Prenatally, in 4 of 21 cases with specialized ultrasound (gestational weeks 12-32), only unspecific cerebellar abnormalities were reported... Prenatal and postnatal ultrasound imaging can fail to detect the condition, with MRI being the gold standard for diagnosis.

evidence.text: Among 42 fetuses prenatally diagnosed with PCH, dedicated neurosonography and fetal MRI were carried out late in gestation (mean gestational ages 29+4 and 31+0 weeks, respectively), and only a minority presented early microcephaly, with biometrics declining late in gestation.

source.title: Prenatal diagnosis of pontocerebellar hypoplasia with postnatal follow‐up
source.quote: Neurosonography and fetal MRI were performed at a mean gestational age of 29 + 4 and 31 + 0 weeks, respectively... Classic PCH is associated with pontine atrophy and small MR measurements decreasing with advancing gestation.

evidence.text: In CASK-related microcephaly with pontocerebellar hypoplasia (MICPCH), prenatal microcephaly (head circumference <-2 SD) was observed in 11 of 19 fetuses at a mean of 20 gestational weeks, illustrating that prenatal biometry varies across atypical or non-classic PCH entities.

source.title: Expanding the natural history of CASK‐related disorders to the prenatal period
source.quote: Information regarding prenatal head circumference was available in 19 patients; 11 out of 19 had a fetal head circumference below -2SD (range -4.1SD to -2.02SD, mean gestational age at diagnosis 20 weeks).

new_directions.question_text: Can advanced fetal MRI tractography of pontine transverse fibers differentiate prenatal PLAA-related disorder from TSEN54-related PCH2 during the third trimester?
new_directions.rationale: While biometric measurements and neurosonography overlap due to normal mid-trimester measurements in both entities, diffusion tractography has shown loss of transverse pontine fibers specifically in PCH2 fetuses.

new_directions.question_text: What specific early infancy movement disorder markers (e.g., choreoathetosis vs spastic tetraparesis) best discriminate PLAA-related disorder from PCH2 prior to genetic turnaround?
new_directions.rationale: PCH2A classically presents with choreathetosis and extrapyramidal dyskinesia in up to 88% of cases, whereas PLAA disorder typically features predominant spasticity without chorea.
